argAssignment: This argument has type "{argType}", but the parameter expects "{paramType}".

argAssignmentParam: Parameter "{paramName}" expects "{paramType}", but this argument has type "{argType}".
argAssignmentParamFunction: "{functionName}" expects "{paramType}" for "{paramName}", but this argument has type "{argType}".
argMissingForParam: The call is missing a required argument for {name}.
argMissingForParams: The call is missing required arguments for {names}.
argMorePositionalExpectedCount: The call needs {expected} additional positional arguments.
argMorePositionalExpectedOne: The call needs one additional positional argument.
argPositionalExpectedCount: This call accepts {expected} positional arguments; check how many you passed.
argPositionalExpectedOne: This call accepts one positional argument; check how many you passed.
paramNameMissing: This function has no parameter named "{name}". Check the keyword spelling and function signature.
paramAlreadyAssigned: "{name}" receives more than one argument, for example both a positional and a keyword argument.
paramAssignmentMismatch: This parameter expects "{paramType}", but the supplied expression has type "{sourceType}".
objectNotCallable: A value of type "{type}" cannot be called with (...). Check whether you meant a function or method.
moduleNotCallable: A module cannot be called with (...). Call the function or class inside the module instead.
noOverload: None of the declared call signatures for "{name}" accepts these arguments. Check their types and names.
typeAssignmentMismatch: This value has type "{sourceType}", but the declared type is "{destType}".
typeAssignmentMismatchWildcard: The imported name "{name}" has type "{sourceType}", but its declaration expects "{destType}".
returnTypeMismatch: This function promises to return "{returnType}", but this return value has type "{exprType}".
returnMissing: This function promises to return "{returnType}", but at least one code path finishes without returning a value.
noReturnReturnsNone: A function annotated NoReturn must not return normally, including returning None.
initMustReturnNone: __init__ initializes an existing instance; it must return None rather than another value.
symbolIsUndefined: Python cannot find a definition of "{name}" in this scope. Check its spelling, definition, or import.
symbolIsUnbound: "{name}" is used before it has a value in this scope.
symbolIsPossiblyUnbound: Some code paths reach this use of "{name}" without assigning it a value.
importResolveFailure: Pyright cannot find "{importName}" in the configured Python environment or import paths. Check the interpreter, installation, and project paths.
importSourceResolveFailure: Pyright found type information for "{importName}", but cannot find its implementation in the configured environment. Check the interpreter and package installation.
importSymbolUnknown: Pyright cannot find an exported name "{name}" in this import. Check the name and installed package version.
stubFileMissing: Pyright cannot find a type stub for "{importName}". The package may work at runtime but lack type information.
importCycleDetected: These modules import each other in a cycle. Check the import chain shown below.
duplicateImport: "{importName}" is imported more than once; one import may be redundant.
memberAccess: Pyright cannot read attribute "{name}" on "{type}". Check its spelling, visibility, and the object's type.
memberSet: Pyright does not allow assigning to attribute "{name}" on "{type}". It may be missing, read-only, or have an incompatible type.
memberDelete: Pyright does not allow deleting attribute "{name}" on "{type}". Check whether deletion is supported.
moduleUnknownMember: Module "{moduleName}" has no known attribute "{memberName}". Check the spelling, exports, and package version.
methodNotDefined: This operation requires the method "{name}", but it is not defined on this value.
methodNotDefinedOnType: This operation requires the method "{name}", but type "{type}" does not implement it.
noneUnknownMember: This value may be None, which has no attribute "{name}". Check for None before accessing it.
noneNotSubscriptable: This value may be None, so indexing it with [...] is unsafe. Check for None before indexing.
noneNotCallable: This value may be None rather than a callable. Check for None before calling it.
noneNotIterable: This value may be None rather than an iterable. Check for None before looping or unpacking.
noneNotUsableWith: This value may be None, which cannot be used as a context manager. Check for None before the with statement.
noneNotUsableWithAsync: This value may be None, which cannot be used as an async context manager. Check for None before async with.
noneOperator: The operator "{operator}" cannot be applied to None here. Check for None before this operation.
typeNotSubscriptable: A value of type "{type}" does not support indexing with [...]. Check the value's type.
tupleIndexOutOfRange: Index {index} is outside the known bounds of tuple type {type}.
typeNotIterable: A value of type "{type}" cannot be iterated over here. Check what you are looping over or unpacking.
typeNotSupportBinaryOperator: The operator "{operator}" cannot combine "{leftType}" and "{rightType}" here.
typeNotSupportBinaryOperatorBidirectiona: The operator "{operator}" cannot combine "{leftType}" and "{rightType}" with the expected result type "{expectedType}".
typeNotSupportUnaryOperator: The operator "{operator}" cannot be applied to "{type}" here.
typeNotSupportUnaryOperatorBidirectional: The operator "{operator}" cannot be applied to "{type}" with the expected result type "{expectedType}".
mixingBytesAndStr: Bytes and text cannot be concatenated directly. Encode text to bytes or decode bytes to text using the appropriate encoding.
unhashableDictKey: Dictionary keys must be hashable. Mutable lists, dictionaries, and sets cannot normally be used as keys.
unhashableSetEntry: Set elements must be hashable. Mutable lists, dictionaries, and sets cannot normally be stored in a set.
unpackedDictArgumentNotMapping: After **, pass a mapping whose keys are strings, so Python can use them as keyword argument names.
dictUnpackIsNotMapping: After ** in a dictionary literal, pass a mapping rather than a sequence or scalar.
tupleAssignmentMismatch: This value of type "{type}" does not match the tuple unpacking target. Check the number and types of its items.
listAssignmentMismatch: This value of type "{type}" does not match the list unpacking target. Check the number and types of its items.
typedDictAccess: This TypedDict lookup is not type-safe. The details below explain whether the key is missing, optional, or invalid.
typedDictSet: This TypedDict assignment is not type-safe. Check the key, value type, and read-only restrictions below.
typedDictDelete: This TypedDict key cannot safely be deleted. Check whether it is required or read-only.
typedDictBadVar: A TypedDict class describes dictionary fields with type annotations; it cannot contain ordinary class statements here.
typedDictBaseClass: A TypedDict can inherit only from other TypedDict classes.
typedDictFieldNotRequiredRedefinition: Inherited field "{name}" cannot be changed to NotRequired here.
typedDictFieldRequiredRedefinition: Inherited field "{name}" cannot be changed to Required here.
typedDictFieldReadOnlyRedefinition: Inherited field "{name}" cannot be changed to ReadOnly here.
awaitNotInAsync: Use await inside an async def function; an ordinary def function cannot await here.
typeNotAwaitable: A value of type "{type}" cannot be awaited. Check whether this call actually returns an awaitable.
unusedCoroutine: This async call creates a coroutine but its result is unused. Await it or pass it to code that runs it.
typeNotUsableWith: "{type}" cannot be used in a with statement because its {method} method is missing or incompatible.
typeNotUsableWithAsync: "{type}" cannot be used in async with because its {method} method is missing or incompatible.
returnInAsyncGenerator: An async generator can yield values, but cannot return a value.
yieldFromOutsideAsync: An async function cannot use yield from. Use async iteration where appropriate.
exceptionTypeIncorrect: "{type}" is not derived from BaseException, so it is not an exception type.
exceptionTypeNotClass: "{type}" cannot be used as an exception class here.
exceptionTypeNotInstantiable: Creating exception "{type}" requires arguments. Supply them when constructing the exception.
expectedExceptionClass: Use an exception class or instance here, rather than an unrelated value.
expectedExceptionObj: An exception cause must be an exception instance, an exception class, or None.
namedExceptAfterCatchAll: A bare except catches everything, so specific except handlers must come before it.
instantiateAbstract: "{type}" still has abstract members and cannot be instantiated. Implement the members listed below in a concrete subclass.
instantiateProtocol: "{type}" is a Protocol describing an interface, not a concrete class to instantiate.
abstractMethodInvocation: Abstract method "{method}" has no implementation to call here.
incompatibleMethodOverride: This override of "{name}" is incompatible with the method in "{className}". Compare the parameter and return types below.
methodOverridden: Override "{name}" in "{className}" has incompatible type "{type}". Check the base method's signature.
propertyOverridden: "{name}" does not correctly override the property in "{className}". Check the getter, setter, and types.
missingSuperCall: "{methodName}" overrides a parent method without calling it. Check whether the parent's initialization or behavior is required.
finalMethodOverride: "{name}" in "{className}" is marked final and must not be overridden.
finalReassigned: "{name}" is annotated Final, so it cannot be assigned a new value.
finalUnassigned: "{name}" is annotated Final but has not been given a value.
constantRedefinition: Pyright treats uppercase name "{name}" as a constant and flags this reassignment. Python itself does not enforce this convention.
privateUsedOutsideOfClass: "{name}" is intended to be private to its declaring class, but is accessed outside it.
privateUsedOutsideOfModule: "{name}" is intended to be private to its declaring module, but is accessed outside it.
protectedUsedOutsideOfClass: "{name}" is intended for use inside its class or subclasses, but is accessed elsewhere.
privateImportFromPyTypedModule: Module "{module}" does not declare "{name}" as a public export. Use its public import path if one exists.
overloadWithoutImplementation: "{name}" has an @overload signature but no runtime implementation in this Python file.
singleOverload: "{name}" has only one @overload signature. Declare alternatives or use an ordinary function signature.
overloadImplementationMismatch: The runtime implementation does not support everything promised by overload {index}.
overloadReturnTypeMismatch: Overloads {prevIndex} and {newIndex} of "{name}" accept overlapping inputs but promise incompatible return types.
overlappingOverload: Overload {obscured} of "{name}" is shadowed by earlier overload {obscuredBy}, so it will never be selected.
typeAnnotationCall: A type annotation needs a type expression, not a function call.
typeAnnotationVariable: This annotation uses a value where Pyright expects a type.
typeCallNotAllowed: Use a type name in this annotation rather than calling type() on a value.
listInAnnotation: Use a type such as list[int] here rather than a list value such as [int].
tupleInAnnotation: Use a tuple type such as tuple[int, str] here rather than a tuple value.
typeArgsMissingForClass: Generic class "{name}" needs type arguments to describe the types it contains or uses.
typeArgsTooFew: "{name}" expects {expected} type arguments, but only {received} were supplied.
typeArgsTooMany: "{name}" expects {expected} type arguments, but {received} were supplied.
typeArgsMismatchOne: This type expects one type argument, but {received} were supplied.
typeArgsExpectingNone: Class "{name}" is not generic here and accepts no type arguments.
typeVarAssignmentMismatch: Type "{type}" does not satisfy the requirements of type variable "{name}".
typeVarNotUsedByOuterScope: Type variable "{name}" is not bound by an enclosing generic function or class in this context.
typeVarUsedOnlyOnce: TypeVar "{name}" appears only once in this function signature, so it does not relate multiple input or output types.
typeVarSingleConstraint: A constrained TypeVar needs at least two alternative types. For one upper limit, use bound= instead.
typeVarBoundAndConstrained: A TypeVar can have a bound or a list of constraints, but not both.
typeVarAssignedName: The variable holding this TypeVar must be named "{name}", matching the TypeVar's declared name.
typeVarVariance: A TypeVar cannot be both covariant and contravariant.
paramTypeCovariant: A covariant TypeVar cannot be used as this input parameter type.
returnTypeContravariant: A contravariant TypeVar cannot be used as this return type.
paramAnnotationMissing: Parameter "{name}" needs a type annotation for this checking mode.
paramTypeUnknown: Pyright cannot determine the type of parameter "{paramName}". Add an annotation or check upstream type information.
paramTypePartiallyUnknown: Part of parameter "{paramName}"'s type is unknown. Check generic arguments and upstream type information.
typeUnknown: Pyright cannot determine the type of "{name}". Check annotations and the source of this value.
typePartiallyUnknown: Part of "{name}"'s type is unknown. Check missing generic arguments and upstream type information.
argTypeUnknown: Pyright cannot determine this argument's type, so it cannot fully check the call.
argTypePartiallyUnknown: Part of this argument's type is unknown, so Pyright cannot fully check the call.
returnTypeUnknown: Pyright cannot determine this function's return type. Check its annotation and returned values.
returnTypePartiallyUnknown: Part of return type "{returnType}" is unknown. Check generic arguments and returned values.
functionDecoratorTypeUnknown: This decorator lacks type information, so Pyright cannot reliably determine how it changes the function's type.
classDecoratorTypeUnknown: This decorator lacks type information, so Pyright cannot reliably determine how it changes the class's type.
baseClassUnknown: The base class lacks type information, so Pyright cannot fully check the derived class.
defaultValueContainsCall: This default value contains a call or mutable object. Defaults are evaluated when the function is defined, not on every call.
assertAlwaysTrue: Pyright considers this assertion always true, so it does not check a condition that could fail here.
assertTypeTypeMismatch: assert_type expects the inferred type to be "{expected}", but Pyright infers "{received}".
comparisonAlwaysFalse: These types, "{leftType}" and "{rightType}", do not overlap, so Pyright considers this condition always false.
comparisonAlwaysTrue: These types, "{leftType}" and "{rightType}", do not overlap, so Pyright considers this condition always true.
matchIsNotExhaustive: This match statement leaves some possible values unhandled. Add cases for the remaining types shown below.
unnecessaryCast: This value already has type "{type}", so this cast does not add type information.
unnecessaryTypeIgnore: This line has no diagnostic needing # type: ignore; the suppression can be removed.
unnecessaryPyrightIgnore: This line has no diagnostic needing # pyright: ignore; the suppression can be removed.
unusedExpression: This expression computes a value but does not use it. Check whether you meant to assign or return it.
unusedCallResult: This call returns "{type}", but the result is unused. Use it or assign it to _ if discarding it is intentional.
unaccessedImport: Import "{name}" is not used in this file. Remove it if it is not needed for exports or side effects.
unaccessedVariable: Variable "{name}" is assigned but never read in this scope.
unaccessedFunction: Function "{name}" is not used in this scope. Check whether it is needed or intended as a public entry point.
unaccessedClass: Class "{name}" is not used in this scope. Check whether it is needed or intended as a public entry point.
unaccessedSymbol: "{name}" is not used in this scope. Check whether it is needed for exports or side effects.
expectedColon: This statement is missing a colon (:), usually before its indented body.
expectedIndentedBlock: This statement needs an indented body. Add its body or use pass as a placeholder.
inconsistentIndent: This line's indentation does not match an earlier block level.
inconsistentTabs: This block mixes tabs and spaces in indentation. Use one consistent indentation style.
unexpectedIndent: This line is indented where Python does not expect a new block.
unexpectedUnindent: This line leaves an indentation level where Python does not expect it.
expectedCloseParen: An opening parenthesis has no matching closing parenthesis.
expectedCloseBracket: An opening square bracket has no matching closing square bracket.
expectedCloseBrace: An opening brace has no matching closing brace.
expectedExpr: Python expects a value or expression here; this part of the statement is incomplete.
expectedAssignRightHandExpr: The assignment is missing a value after =.
expectedBinaryRightHandExpr: This operator is missing the expression on its right-hand side.
expectedMemberName: The dot must be followed by an attribute or method name.
expectedFunctionName: Add a function name after def.
expectedClassName: Add a class name after class.
expectedImportSymbols: Add one or more names after import.
unexpectedEof: The file ends before this statement is complete. Check missing brackets, quotes, or a required body.
unexpectedExprToken: This expression has an unexpected token at its end. Check for an extra symbol or missing separator.
breakOutsideLoop: A break statement must be inside a loop.
continueOutsideLoop: A continue statement must be inside a loop.
returnOutsideFunction: A return statement must be inside a function.
yieldOutsideFunction: A yield expression must be inside a function or lambda.
matchIncompatible: Pattern matching needs Python 3.10 or newer. Check Pyright's configured Python version.
typeAliasStatementIllegal: The type alias statement needs Python 3.12 or newer. Check Pyright's configured Python version.
functionTypeParametersIllegal: This generic function syntax needs Python 3.12 or newer. Check Pyright's configured Python version.
